answer: A sybil assault resembles a sudden volatility mismatch across a liquidity bridge where agents exploit mispriced issuance. To suppress cheap node creation, the system forces each agent to burn an unrecoverable ember of staked capital to open a secured execution channel. This collateral acts like a digital yarrow stalk that decays via time-weighted vega decay, making long-term attacks mathematically unprofitable while preserving market maker spread.
